transcript:
Meeting header: 2029-04-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Recorded on Fireflies
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SA); Maya Chen (VP Product, Lucent Bridge), Arjun Patel (Lead Systems Engineer), Sophie Laurent (Partnerships), Tomás Rivera (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick partner discovery to evaluate Lucent Bridge as a channel/reseller + integration onramp for cloud GPU capacity and private deployments. Focus areas: throughput SLA, KV cache/latency work, routing and fallbacks, security and KMS, pilot scope and success criteria.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, uh, welcome. I'm Jordan Kim, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. Thanks for taking the time.
[00:15] Maya: Hi Jordan, thanks. I'm Maya, VP Product at Lucent Bridge. Excited to see how this works.
[00:22] Priya: Hi, Priya Nair here, I'm the SE working with Jordan on integration patterns and benching.
[00:30] Arjun: Arjun Patel, I'll be the eng lead on the Lucent side. We manage the onramp and the infra.
[00:37] Sophie: Sophie from Partnerships — quick note, we're mostly focused on reseller economics and GTM overlap.
[00:43] Jordan: Great — quick agenda: 1) high level goals and timeline 2) security/compliance 3) technical patterns for hybrid routing and on-prem, 4) pilot success metrics and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:55] Maya: Yep that's perfect.

[01:12] Priya: To start — can you give us the broad use cases you want Redwood to enable via the Lucent onramp? Is this primarily white-labeled hosted access or a private deployment for clients?
[01:30] Maya: A mix. Our channel customers want a hosted offering we can resell, but our enterprise accounts ask for VPC/private stacks. We were thinking Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and then Redwood Private for a small number of sensitive customers. Ideally same API surface.
[01:50] Jordan: That aligns well with our product. Dedicated for reserved capacity, Private if they need VPC/on-prem. We often recommend starting with a hosted API pilot to validate UX then expand to dedicated or private. Note: routing between tiers is something we can configure.

[02:14] Arjun: Two constraints: latency SLOs under 120ms p95 for small prompt flows, and cold-start token cost. Also we need a clear path for KV cache — we saw some notes in your docs but want to understand operational impact.
[02:35] Priya: Yeah, KV cache — sometimes transcribed as K V cash — is critical. For low-latency chat workloads we use prefix caching and shard KV across GPUs, that reduces repeated prefix cost by up to 6x in our internal tests. But there are tradeoffs when you mix dedicated and hosted backends.
[02:58] Arjun: Right, and our question is how stateful caches work across Lucent customers when we resell — isolation, eviction policy, and how that interacts with autoscaling.

[03:20] Priya: For resellers we offer per-customer namespaces and optional sticky routing to a pool. Autoscaling is compatible but to meet strict p95 SLOs you might reserve capacity (Dedicated) for the high-value accounts. Otherwise we can route to a warm fallback model for overflow.

[03:45] Sophie: On the commercial side, we want clear unit economics — how batching, quantization, and routing policies affect our margin. Do you have recommended starter configs for reseller pilots?
[03:58] Jordan: We usually propose a two-tier pilot: one hosted public plan for low-touch customers and one Dedicated pool for two enterprise accounts. We'll share a pricing matrix — look at per-token with dedicated commit offsets — and a margin calculator.

[04:18] Tomás: Security — SOC2 is table stakes. We also need key management with customer KMS (HSM preferred). Can Redwood hand off keys or support our KMS integration?
[04:33] Jordan: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted and Dedicated we also offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys in the private plane. We'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 report.

[04:50] Priya: Quick note — for on-prem or VPC deployments there's a lightweight control plane and a customer managed data path. That gives you the KMS hooks and audit logs you asked about. But there are extra ops responsibilities.

[05:07] Arjun: How does log retention and audit logging look? We need per-tenant audit trails for compliance customers.
[05:16] Jordan: Per-route and token-level tracing in the Console, retention is configurable as an add-on. We'll send the retention tiers and pricing.

[05:30] [Speaker 2]: (unclear)  sorry can you repeat the part about auto-scale policy?
[05:36] Priya: Sure, autoscaling can be proactive or reactive, you can set a target p95 and we can scale based on token rate or active connections. There's also burst capacity for short spikes.

[06:02] Maya: One of our customers uses very long-context multi-turn workflows. We need guidance on sequence length costs and whether dynamic kv eviction will cause correctness issues.
[06:20] Priya: For long contexts we suggest model variants and quantization profiles, and strategic prefix caching — the runtime will pick kernels optimized for long sequences, but cost rises roughly linearly with sequence length. We'll propose a model mapping doc.

[06:45] Jordan: On the legal/commercial lane — Sophie, you said Lucent would prefer a reseller margin + co-sell motion. We can do revenue share or referral for initial pilots. What's ideal?
[06:58] Sophie: Revenue share is preferred, but we can start with referral credits. Need to lock in pricing bands so our sales team can package it.

[07:12] Arjun: Tech deep dive — Priya, can we run a bench with our payloads? We'll toss you sample prompts and simulated qps, want to see latency breakdown (inference vs network vs queuing).
[07:26] Priya: Absolutely. We'll need sample payloads and realistic concurrency patterns. Preferably a 48 hour run with both warm and cold starts. We'll script it and share a runbook.

[07:40] Jordan: I'll add that to next steps. Also we'll include an integration pattern doc showing sticky routing, fallback to smaller models, and canary rollout flow.

[08:00] Maya: Ok early timeline — target pilot start in May, run through June, decision by July. Is that feasible?
[08:10] Jordan: Feasible. Pilot prep in April (deck + security Q), bench in late April/early May, pilot kick-off mid-May. We'll make a timeline and share a Gantt.

[08:25] [09:00] (speaker labeling drifts)
[09:00] Tomás: A couple of security specifics: do you speak to encryption-in-flight algorithms, and do you support customer-side TLS termination?
[09:12] Priya: We support TLS everywhere, mutual TLS for Private, and customer-side termination can be accommodated in the VPC setup. For algorithm specifics, we'll provide details — AES-256, RSA or ECDSA for key exchange, and HSM-backed KMS where required.

[10:00] Jordan: Are there any blockers from your side that would prevent starting a bench?
[10:07] Arjun: Two blockers: 1) We need a non-prod pricing estimate to budget the bench. 2) We need the security questionnaire answered.
[10:16] Jordan: We'll push a non-prod bench estimate and the security packet after the call.

[12:00] Priya: On the integration itself — we suggest three patterns: 1) direct reseller proxy (Lucent proxies to Redwood-hosted APIs), 2) Dedicated pool per reseller with tenant namespaces, 3) Private on-prem installation for strategic accounts. Each has pros/cons on ops and latency.
[12:24] Arjun: For pattern 1, how do you handle rate limiting and fair usage across multi-tenant reseller traffic?
[12:34] Priya: Rate limits per token and per API key, and per-namespace quotas. For reseller proxy we also recommend token-level attribution so you can bill downstream customers correctly.

[13:00] Sophie: Product question — how much work is required on our side to integrate billing attribution into our existing invoicing system?
[13:10] Jordan: We have webhooks and CSV exports; we can also offer a billing API. We'll map the fields you need, but expect one to two sprints of engineering for deeper integration.

[14:00] Maya: Can Redwood run confidentiality-assured bench on our anonymized data? Some of our prompts contain PII.
[14:12] Priya: Yes — we can run tests on anonymized payloads. For Private we can keep data fully within your VPC. For hosted bench we treat test data under NDA and will delete after the run.

[15:00] Arjun: Small nit — we saw a note about kernel selection and were wondering how automatic that is. Do you need us to tune anything?
[15:10] Priya: Kernel selection is automatic in the runtime; it chooses optimized kernels by model architecture and sequence length. The only tuning we usually need is quantization profile choice for a model if you want lower memory/latency tradeoffs.

[16:00] [16:22] Jordan: Any questions on commercial SLAs? We typically offer a 99.9% uptime SLA on Dedicated and enterprise packages.
[16:33] Sophie: That would be acceptable. How about latency SLOs tied to model class?
[16:40] Jordan: We can tie p95 latency SLOs per-route and model. We'll include example SLOs in the pricing doc.

[17:00] Maya: Ok, pilot success criteria — what should we mutually agree on?
[17:08] Priya: I'd propose 1) p95 latency less than 120ms for designated flows, 2) accuracy/regression thresholds on key prompts (we'll provide eval harness), 3) cost per 1k tokens within expected bounds, and 4) operational readiness (runbook and oncall).
[17:28] Arjun: For evals, can we run regression tests against our existing in-house model so we can show parity or uplift?
[17:36] Priya: Yes, we'll run side-by-side evaluations. We'll ask for a small prompt set and acceptance thresholds.

[18:00] Tomás: Data residency — some EU customers require compute in EU only. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[18:10] Jordan: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Private on-prem it's obviously local. For hosted we have EU regions and can pin traffic. We'll note the extra cost for region isolation.

[19:00] [19:10] Maya: Quick commercial ask — do you offer trial credits or partner discounts for early pilots?
[19:18] Jordan: Yes, we typically provide credits and a partner discount for an initial pilot. We'll include specific numbers in the deck.

[20:00] Arjun: A technical question — how do you handle KV eviction across GPU restarts and node failures? We saw some notes but want the failure modes documented.
[20:12] Priya: The KV cache is mostly in-memory on the serving nodes; we persist critical segments for longer-term reuse depending on configuration. On restarts we have a warmup prefetch and fallback to model recomputation. We'll share a failure mode doc.

[22:00] Sophie: From GTM, what's the typical time to revenue for partners that do a pilot?
[22:10] Jordan: Usually 3-6 months from pilot start to first paid deal, depends on your pipeline. We'll include case studies.

[24:00] [24:20] (brief cross-talk)
[24:30] Maya: Are there any limits on model variants we can expose to our customers?
[24:37] Priya: You can expose multiple model variants; routing policies can map customers to variants by tier. We can also automate fallback to cheaper variants when capacity is constrained.

[26:00] Arjun: For the bench run, what telemetry will you provide? Specifically token-level breakdown, kernel times, GPU utl, and queue times.
[26:12] Priya: We'll provide per-request traces (sampled), token-level latency breakdowns, GPU utilization, and our console dashboards. We'll also provide raw logs for analysis.

[28:00] Tomás: On audit — do you keep immutable audit logs for queries? Some of our compliance requires tamper-evident logs.
[28:12] Jordan: We can provide append-only logs with signed entries for Private deployments; for hosted/Dedicated there's enterprise options. We'll surface the exact support levels in the security packet.

[30:00] [30:10] Priya: Ok, let's align on a minimal bench plan: 1) 48 hour run, 2) 10k simulated concurrent users in waves up to target qps, 3) mix of short and long contexts, 4) sample prompt set of ~150 prompts. We can tune from there.

[31:00] Arjun: We'll provide payloads and a concurrency profile. Can we also test model variant switching mid-run?
[31:10] Priya: Yes, we'll script canary transitions and record impact.

[33:00] Jordan: Commercially, we'll send a non-prod estimate for the bench and a pilot pricing proposal after the security doc.

[35:00] Maya: Any other concerns — latency, security, billing are the big three.
[35:08] Sophie: Also ops overhead for us, we need to know how much engineering for attribution and billing.

[36:00] Priya: We'll provide an integration effort estimate — usually 2-4 sprints for a deep billing integration; webhook/CSV is much faster.

[38:00] [38:12] (brief pause)
[38:30] Tomás: A compliance nuance — some of our clients require FIPS 140-2 compatible crypto. Is that supported?
[38:40] Jordan: We have FIPS-compatible options in our Private and Dedicated packages. We'll note requirements for HSM and certs.

[40:00] Arjun: Let's list the artifacts we need to move forward so we can close blockers: 1) Partner deck 2) Security packet + SOC2 3) Non-prod bench estimate 4) Sample payload format for bench 5) Draft MOU/pilot scope.
[40:20] Jordan: Agreed — we'll deliver those.

[42:00] Priya: For the bench, please provide a sample of PII-masked prompts and a concurrency CSV. We'll choreograph the runs and give you SSH access to the runner for log pulls.

[44:00] Sophie: On the partnership model, we may want joint case study language. We'll work with your marketing.

[45:00] Jordan: Good. Any outstanding technical risks you want on the table now?
[45:10] Arjun: We care about cold start degradation when autoscaling and cost predictability if we route to multiple models.

[46:00] Priya: We'll demonstrate warmup strategies and fallback routing in the bench, and we'll show cost estimates with batching and quantization on.

[48:00] Maya: Ok, last thing — can we schedule the tech deep dive next week for inner-loop details?
[48:10] Jordan: Yes, suggest dates. We'll propose 2029-04-24 or 25.

[50:00] [50:12] (crosstalk)
[50:30] Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan to send deck and non-prod estimate; Priya to prepare bench plan and scripts; Arjun to provide payloads and QPS profile; Tomás to share security questionnaire answers — target dates as captured in action items.

[52:00] Maya: This was helpful. Looking forward to the bench.
[52:12] Sophie: We'll also line up our GTM contacts.

[54:00] [54:15] (wrap)
[54:20] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the shared links.
[54:30] Priya: Thanks all.
[54:35] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional speaker label drift, some acronyms transcribed imperfectly (K V cash for KV cache, K-M-SH for KMS/HSM). Security docs referenced but not attached — links above.
